responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for the OpenRISC (or1k) architecture, covering both the core machine description used during RTL expansion, instruction selection, scheduling, and assembly emission and the target-environment variants used by the driver for bare-metal ELF, GNU/Linux, and RTEMS. Its main backend files define the OpenRISC machine model and ABI—registers, data layout, calling convention, stack/frame rules, PIC and exception-handling details—then implement target hooks for frame layout, prologue/epilogue generation, argument passing, address legitimacy, atomics, trampolines, operand printing, and other OpenRISC-specific RTL lowering logic. The declarative instruction-selection side is carried by the machine description together with predicate and constraint families that describe valid operands, immediates, register classes, delay-slot and scheduling behavior, and the instruction patterns for arithmetic, floating point, control flow, calls, and atomic operations. Companion option files define OpenRISC ISA and code-model switches and the generated metadata behind them, while the environment headers customize preprocessor builtins, linker specs, runtime start/end files, board selection, and dynamic-linker behavior for the different OpenRISC operating environments.
